arxiv-2101-05907.title: Bohm potential for the time dependent harmonic oscillator
arxiv-2101-05907.creator: Francisco Soto-Eguibar, Felipe A. Asenjo, Sergio A. Hojman, Héctor M. Moya-Cessa
arxiv-2101-05907.description: Abstract In the Madelung-Bohm approach to quantum mechanics, we consider a (time dependent) phase that depends quadratically on position and show that it leads to a Bohm potential that corresponds to a time dependent harmonic oscillator, provided the time dependent term in the phase obeys an Ermakov equation. aff1]Instituto Nacional de Astrofísica, Óptica y Electrónica, Calle Luis Enrique Erro No.

arxiv-2202-09330.title: Integer Conformal Dimensions for Type IIA Flux Vacua
arxiv-2202-09330.creator: Fien Apers, Joseph P. Conlon, Sirui Ning, Filippo Revello
arxiv-2202-09330.description: Abstract We give a concise argument that supersymmetric AdS type IIA DGKT flux vacua on general Calabi-Yaus have, interpreted holographically, integer conformal dimensions for low-lying scalar primaries in the dual CFT. These integers are independent of any compactification details, such as the background fluxes or triple intersection numbers of the compact manifold.

arxiv-2207-04398.title: Self-supervised Learning with Local Contrastive Loss for Detection and Semantic Segmentation
arxiv-2207-04398.creator: Ashraful Islam, Ben Lundell, Harpreet Sawhney, Sudipta N. Sinha, Peter Morales, Richard J. Radke
arxiv-2207-04398.description: Abstract We present a self-supervised learning (SSL) method suitable for semi-global tasks such as object detection and semantic segmentation. We enforce local consistency between self-learned features that represent corresponding image locations of transformed versions of the same image, by minimizing a pixel-level local contrastive (LC) loss during training. LC-loss can be added to existing self-supervised learning methods with minimal overhead.

arxiv-2407-17114.title: A Self-Supervised Image Registration Approach for Measuring Local Response Patterns in Metastatic Ovarian Cancer
arxiv-2407-17114.creator: Inês P. Machado* (🖂), Anna Reithmeir, Fryderyk Kogl, Leonardo Rundo, Gabriel Funingana, Marika Reinius, Gift Mungmeeprued, Zeyu Gao, Cathal McCague, Eric Kerfoot, Ramona Woitek, Evis Sala, Yangming Ou, James Brenton, Julia Schnabel, Mireia Crispin
arxiv-2407-17114.description: Abstract High-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC) is characterised by significant spatial and temporal heterogeneity, typically manifesting at an advanced metastatic stage. A major challenge in treating advanced HGSOC is effectively monitoring localised change in tumour burden across multiple sites during neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) and predicting long-term pathological response and overall patient survival.

arxiv-2602-08874.title: Is Reasoning Capability Enough for Safety in Long-Context Language Models?
arxiv-2602-08874.creator: Yu Fu, Haz Sameen Shahgir, Huanli Gong, Zhipeng Wei, N. Benjamin Erichson, Yue Dong
arxiv-2602-08874.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) increasingly combine long-context processing with advanced reasoning, enabling them to retrieve and synthesize information distributed across tens of thousands of tokens. A hypothesis is that stronger reasoning capability should improve safety by helping models recognize harmful intent even when it is not stated explicitly.

pmc-10641310.title: Protocol to visualize glycan-mediated binding between virus and human blood mononuclear cells using thin-section transmission electron microscopy
pmc-10641310.creator: Belinda L Spillings, Kathryn Green, Erica Lovas, Richard Webb, Johnson Mak
pmc-10641310.description: SummaryGlycan-glycan interactions between viral particles and host cells may lengthen the dwell time of the virus on the cell surface to facilitate cellular receptor engagement. Here, we present a protocol for visualizing glycan-mediated binding between virus or virus-like-particles (VLPs) and human peripheral blood mononuclear cells using transmission electron microscopy (TEM).

pmc-11312811.title: Impact of Idiopathic Scoliosis on the Cardiopulmonary Capacity of Adolescents
pmc-11312811.creator: Andrzej Siwiec, Małgorzata Domagalska-Szopa, Ilona Kwiecień-Czerwieniec, Agata Dobrowolska, Andrzej Szopa, Francesco Giallauria
pmc-11312811.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Chest deformities in children with scoliosis may result in cardiopulmonary disorders, lowering cardiopulmonary capacity levels. However, results regarding the dependence of cardiopulmonary capacity on the severity level of scoliosis remain controversial. We aimed to use dynamic cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) to investigate exercise capacity in reference to spinal deformity in patients with mild or moderate idiopathic scoliosis by means of multivariate analyses. Methods: We included 92 children and adolescents aged 10–17 years with mild and moderate idiopathic scoliosis and 94 healthy peers.

pmc-12630064.title: A novel approach for migraine detection using localized component filtering and electroencephalographic spectral asymmetry index
pmc-12630064.creator: Samaneh Alsadat Saeedinia, Mohammad Reza Jahed-Motlagh, Abbas Tafakhori
pmc-12630064.description: Background: This study aims to improve the accuracy and reliability of migraine detection by combining the localized component filtering (LCF) method with the electroencephalographic (EEG) spectral asymmetry index (SASI) method. The integration of LCF and SASI in the frequency domain under 3 Hz photic stimulation offers a novel approach for robust classification.

pmc-12756478.title: A warming-yang herbal decoction protects against high-altitude hypoxia–induced osteoblast injury through modulation of HIF-1 signaling
pmc-12756478.creator: Xuehai Liu, Yaqian Qi, Rui Zhao, Binkui Jia, Xilin Lei, Hongfan Li, Di Wang, Haoling Zhang, Wei Wang, Zhijing Song
pmc-12756478.description: ObjectiveThis paper systematically explored dental osteoblast injury at high altitude hypoxic condition and examined the protective role of warming-yang traditional medicine, Aconitum carm michaelii and Zingiber officinale decoction (GAWD) in this condition.MethodsWe constructed an in-situ high-altitude hypoxic model (4,500 m) with MC3T3-E1 osteoblastic cells and conducted RNA-seq analysis for Differentially Expressed Genes (DEGs).

pmc-12821204.title: Dysregulated autophagy in endometriosis: molecular mechanisms, controversies, and clinical implications
pmc-12821204.creator: Clara Tellez-Quijorna, Ainhoa Juan-Lopez, Nuria Eritja, David Llobet-Navas, Laura Devis-Jauregui
pmc-12821204.description: Endometriosis is one of the most common gynecological diseases in women and is still one of the most understudied diseases, affecting the daily lives of patients. Although the exact cause of this condition remains unclear, autophagy has been proposed as a potential biological process involved in the disease.

pmc-13094568.title: Impact of Transfusion Dependence on Clinical and Economic Burden in Patients with Lower-Risk Myelodysplastic Syndromes: A 28-Year Retrospective Study
pmc-13094568.creator: Jun Ho Jang, Chul Won Jung, Dae-Ho Choi, Ji-Hyun Kim, Kyungah Lee, Hyojin Kim
pmc-13094568.description: BackgroundMyelodysplastic syndromes comprise a diverse group of hematopoietic stem-cell malignancies characterized by ineffective hematopoiesis, cytopenia, and increased risk of acute myeloid leukemia. Anemia is a common manifestation of lower-risk myelodysplastic syndrome (LR-MDS) and often necessitates red blood cell (RBC) transfusions, although reliance on transfusions is associated with adverse outcomes and substantial burden.

pmc-13239105.title: Concurrent Tongue and Cervical Lymph Node Amyloidosis Without Systemic Disease
pmc-13239105.creator: Chelsea O Onyeji, Alycia M Boutrand, Lewis Overton
pmc-13239105.description: Amyloidosis of the head and neck is often associated with systemic involvement. However, this report describes a rare presentation of localized amyloidosis involving both the tongue and cervical lymph nodes in a patient without systemic disease. It highlights the importance of a thorough workup in differentiating amyloidosis from metastatic malignancy.

pmc-13669210.creator: Mariia S. Kiseleva, Tytti Kärki, Mika Latikka, Parham Koochak, Sakari Lepikko, Maja Vuckovac, Tomi Koskinen, Ramesh Raju, Ville P. Jokinen, Jiazheng Liu, Nenad Miljkovic, Jaakko V. I. Timonen, Ilkka Tittonen, Robin H. A. Ras
pmc-13669210.description: Water condensation on superhydrophobic surfaces can generate spontaneous droplet jumping, enabling rapid condensate removal and improved thermal and mass transfer. Although this effect has been extensively demonstrated on densely packed nanostructures, the capability of microscale textures to support jumping condensation remains poorly understood.
